Review Guidance

Source: REVIEW.md

Read by every automated and human review of this repository. It defines what counts as a failure here — findings outside it are noise.

What this package is

ggseg.formats defines the ggseg_atlas S3 class and the contract that the whole ggsegverse ecosystem is built on: ggseg, ggseg3d, ggseg.extra, and every atlas package consume it. A change that breaks the contract breaks dozens of packages at once, and you find out from CRAN’s automated mail with a deadline attached. Treat the contract as published API, not as internal structure.

What counts as a failure

Report these as Important:

  • A change to the ggseg_atlas contract — required columns, their types, allowed values of type/hemi/side, or the structure of the nested geometry columns — without a lifecycle deprecation path
  • An S3 method added, removed, or narrowed for a class the package already supports. as_ggseg_atlas, atlas_display, atlas_hemi, atlas_labels, atlas_regions, and atlas_type each dispatch on brain_atlas, data.frame, ggseg_atlas, and ggseg3d_atlas; dropping one of those silently is a break
  • Wrong results returned silently — a region renamed, dropped, reordered, or mapped to the wrong hemisphere while the object still validates
  • A bundled atlas (dk, aseg, tracula, suit) whose region count, labels, or palette no longer match its source
  • legacy_region_map changes that remap an existing label, rather than only adding new ones — that silently rewrites other people’s published figures
  • An exported function’s signature, defaults, or return type changing without deprecation
  • A new branch or changed behaviour with no test exercising it
  • A new hard dependency in Imports that isn’t justified in the PR description. The package deliberately keeps sf in Suggests — moving it, or making any code path require it unconditionally, is a break (see R/sf_availability.R)
  • Locale- or platform-dependent behaviour in region sorting or label comparison
  • Anything that makes R CMD check fail or adds a CRAN NOTE

What is not a failure

Do not report:

  • Style, naming, or formatting — air and lintr own those and run in code-quality.yaml
  • Missing roxygen on internal (non-exported) helpers
  • Hypotheticals without a concrete atlas or input that triggers them
  • Performance opinions without a measured cost on a realistic atlas. Atlas objects are tens of thousands of rows, so a measured claim is welcome and an unmeasured one is not
  • Pre-existing issues outside the diff, unless the diff makes them materially worse — tag those Pre-existing and keep them to one line each

Evidence standard

Every finding cites file:line and a concrete failure scenario: a named atlas or specific input → the wrong output. A claim you cannot anchor to a line is not a finding.

Nit budget

At most 3 nits per review. If there are more, report the three that matter and drop the rest.

Paths to skip

  • man/ — generated by roxygen2
  • NAMESPACE — generated by roxygen2
  • README.md — generated from README.Rmd
  • docs/, inst/doc/ — generated by pkgdown
  • data/*.rda binaries — review data-raw/ instead, which produces them

Paths that always get full depth

Regardless of how small the diff looks:

  • R/core_contract.R, R/ggseg_atlas.R, R/validation.R — the contract itself
  • R/coercion.R, R/compat_dataframe.R — how every other package enters and leaves it
  • R/legacy_region_map.R — remapping is retroactive
  • R/sysdata.rda, data-raw/ — shipped data
  • DESCRIPTION — dependencies, and the sf-in-Suggests boundary
  • .github/workflows/ — a broken gate is worse than a broken function
